subject: ventures/tender-bid-readiness
professional: a senior capture / proposal manager who runs bid/no-bid on US federal and state construction solicitations (APMP-trained). They would check first that a bid-guarantee or bond requirement written in FAR 52.228-1 language is caught, that the bid deadline is not confused with the question deadline, that amendments (SF 30) and a mandatory site visit are flagged, and that set-aside / size-standard eligibility is checked

evidence.correctness: Ran check.mjs (identical to the served https://marisstella.app/tender-bid-readiness/check.mjs) on FAR clause text fetched from acquisition.gov (52.228-1, 52.228-15, 52.236-27, 52.214-7, 52.215-1, 52.204-7) and on hand-written standard solicitation sentences, with expected results from reading the text as a capture manager would. Passes: 52.228-15 performance/payment bonds found, 52.236-27 site visit found, 52.204-7 SAM registration found (3). Failures: 52.228-1(a)+(c) bid guarantee requirement scores 0 (bond missed because the FAR says 'bid guarantee'); the full 52.228-1 scores 43% with insurance found inside 'coinsurance' and certification on 'certified check'; 52.214-7(a) deadline evidence is the single word 'due.'; with a question deadline before the bid deadline the question date is shown as the submission deadline; 'received no later than', 'publicly opened at' and 'acknowledge ... amendments ... SF 30' all score 0; negations ('A bid bond is not required', 'No site visit will be held') count as found; 'Due to' counts as a deadline. 3 pass, 1 partial, 5 fail of 9 recomputed rows. False positives are cheap (an excerpt is shown); the false negatives on federal standard vocabulary are not. 1.
evidence.completeness: Every feature README and page name works end to end: paste, Check readiness, seven signals with action text and evidence excerpt, Clear, '% signal coverage' with the 'Green means a phrase was found' caveat, local-only usage counter honoring DNT/GPC with the opt-out persisted, guide and vs pages, links to existing sibling ventures (tender-radar, rfp-compliance-matrix, contractor-bid-readiness), sitemap/robots. No TODOs or stubs. Served page, llms.txt and vs page return 200. 3.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/tender-bid-readiness && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 16 tests, 16 pass, 0.13 s. Only 4 tests touch check.mjs, all on the author's own phrasing; the rest are page-string greps. quality_mutate.py on check.mjs: 2 of 6 mutants caught (insurance alternative removed; site-visit alternative removed); survived: performance/payment bond dropped from the bond rule, bare 'due' dropped from the deadline rule, Math.round -> Math.floor in the score, and the all-found warning boundary off by one. No test uses real solicitation text. 1.
evidence.craft: Read check.mjs (27 lines), index.html script, all three test files. The engine is a list of seven case-insensitive regexes with String.match: no word boundaries (\bdue\b, insurance inside coinsurance), first match only, no negation handling, no handling of the FAR vocabulary, the evidence window cut at a newline. Page script is minified one-liners with mixed indentation in the preference IIFE (index.html:33-34); escapeHtml used correctly on all output. Small and readable, but the matching is naive for its job. 2.
evidence.claims: Backed: local-only processing (no fetch in check.mjs or index.html script, usage counter writes localStorage only), disclaimers (No warranty and no-SLA on index, guide, vs page and README), 'heuristic' and 'green means found, not satisfied' caveats, GovWin IQ identity (Deltek's own page: 'Find Leads First', forecasting, agency history, competitive context, SLED/Canada), non-affiliation line, no invented price. Not backed or unfair: vs-govwin.html:54 says reading one solicitation's requirements 'is not that platform's job' and :34 'This checker does none of what GovWin IQ does', and the table routes the go/no-go question to this checker alone, while Deltek's page markets 'Dela AI ... summarize documents, and score lead fit', 'Smart Fit Scores' and 'go/no-go decisions'; the index FAQ's 'within 100 characters of a match' misdescribes the matcher; llms.txt says 'numbers typed in'; the vs page publishes an internal note that pricing was 'not reachable from this session'. 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a small contractor pastes a federal construction IFB built from standard FAR clauses. The checklist of seven things to verify is a useful reminder, but on the FAR's own wording the bond finding can read 'Not found' (bid guarantee), amendments are not flagged, the deadline excerpt can be the question deadline or the single word 'due.', and set-aside eligibility is not mentioned. Spurious matches raise the percentage, so the score is not a usable signal. A contractor still has to read the whole notice for exactly the items the tool lists. Usable as a printed checklist, not as an extractor. 2.
evidence.domain: A senior capture/proposal manager (APMP practice) separates a compliance gate (eligibility, set-aside and size standard, SAM/UEI, bonding capacity, insurance, licences, mandatory site visit, amendment acknowledgement, deadlines, submission method) from the scored bid/no-bid (customer, competition, capability, past performance, price-to-win). The tool covers part of the gate and none of the scoring, which the README states. Within the gate it misses the FAR terms (bid guarantee per FAR 28.101/52.228-1, amendment per 52.214-3/15.208, time set for receipt/bid opening per 52.214-7 and 14.402) and has no set-aside, acceptance-period or wage-determination signal. The guide page's practice advice (two deadlines, additional insured, surety relationship) is sound but not implemented. 2.

defects.what: Misses the FAR's own wording for core requirements: a bid-guarantee requirement worded as FAR 52.228-1(a)/(c) ('bid guarantee', no 'bid bond') scores 0; amendment acknowledgement ('amendments', SF 30) is not a questions/addenda signal; 'must be received no later than' and 'publicly opened at' are not deadlines. A user reads 'Not found: bond' on a federal IFB that requires one

Only the first match per signal is kept, so with 'Questions must be submitted by 1 December' before 'Bids are due 15 December' the deadline finding shows the question deadline; the guide page's own 'two deadlines, not one' rule is not implemented

No word boundaries or negation: 'coinsurance' -> insurance, 'certified check' and 'certified payroll' -> certification, 'Due to site constraints' -> deadline, 'A bid bond is not required' and 'No site visit will be held' -> found; all raise the coverage percentage. FAR 52.228-1 alone scores 43% with 2 of 3 findings spurious

Tests only use the author's own phrasing; 4 of 6 seeded mutations survive, including dropping performance/payment bond detection and dropping bare 'due' from the deadline rule, and the partial-coverage score and the all-found warning boundary are untested

vs-govwin.html says reading one solicitation's requirements 'is not that platform's job' and that this checker 'does none of what GovWin IQ does' while routing go/no-go to this checker; Deltek's GovWin IQ page (2026-11-12) markets Dela AI document summaries, Smart Fit Scores and go/no-go decision support. The comparison understates the competitor
No signal for small-business set-aside / NAICS size-standard eligibility, bid acceptance period or wage determinations, which a capture manager checks first on a US public bid

FAQ says patterns are matched 'within 100 characters of a match'; the 100 characters are only the evidence excerpt after the keyword, cut at a newline (a FAR 52.214-7(a) deadline excerpt is just 'due.'). llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' for a text tool. vs-govwin.html tells the public that pricing was 'not reachable from this session'

verdict: A seven-regex keyword checker that does what its page says it does (paste, seven signals with excerpts, local only, honest heuristic caveats, full disclaimers), but its outputs are not reliable on real solicitation language. On FAR clause text fetched from acquisition.gov, a bid-guarantee requirement worded as FAR 52.228-1(a)/(c) scores 0, the full clause scores 43% with two spurious findings ('coinsurance', 'certified check'), amendment acknowledgement and 'received no later than' deadlines are missed, negations count as found, and the question deadline is shown as the bid deadline when it comes first. 4 of 6 seeded mutations survive the 16 tests. The GovWin IQ comparison is accurate on identity but omits Deltek's own advertised document summaries, fit scoring and go/no-go support while saying reading a solicitation is not that platform's job. Does not meet the bar (correctness 1, verification 1, claims 2, median 2); finished at its own stated scope (completeness 3).
